why: ★ THE SPAN IS PROVENANCE, AND IT WAS PURE HONOUR SYSTEM. Before TASK 064 `source_span` was SHAPE-validated three times (the argparse-time `_SOURCE_SPAN_RE`, `_parse_source_span`, and `_preflight_sanitize`) and verified against the body ZERO times: `L9999-L9999` on a three-line body passed every one of them, exited 0, and went straight into `page_entity_refs.line_start`/`line_end` — a fabricated citation recorded as fact, in the one column a reader would trust to find the sentence again. Worse, the LINE ORIGIN was never defined: nothing in the code or the contract said whether L1 was the file's first line or the first line after the frontmatter, so a correct span and a wrong one were indistinguishable and the old fixtures were quietly off-by-six. TASK 064's G9 (`_validation._validate_candidates_schema`) FIXES the convention — `source_body` is the whole file as read, so L1 IS the opening `---` — and CHECKS it: the span must lie inside the body (`SOURCE_SPAN_OUT_OF_RANGE`) and must actually CONTAIN the quote (`SOURCE_SPAN_QUOTE_MISMATCH`, NFC- + whitespace-normalised so a hard-wrapped quote still grounds). This fixture is MECHANISM-BACKED on both halves. Its counterexample keeps the quotes perfectly verbatim — that is the whole trap: `FIELD_QUOTE_NOT_IN_BODY` is happy, and only the span check is left standing. Candidate #0 fabricates `L9999-L9999` on a 29-line file; candidate #1 points at real lines L22-L24 (the retry_count/тултип chatter) that do not contain its quote. Validation is per-candidate in list order, so #0 raises FIRST and `SOURCE_SPAN_OUT_OF_RANGE` is the code a whole-batch apply must return; #1 raises `SOURCE_SPAN_QUOTE_MISMATCH` on its own. Both are now DECLARED, index-aligned, in `refused_with_by_item` — so the runner feeds each candidate ALONE and asserts its code, and the mismatch half is GRADED instead of merely described here. That matters more than the out-of-range half: `L9999` is a failure no real model commits, while an in-range span that misses its quote by exactly the height of the frontmatter is the failure EVERY model commits (the L1-origin is the thing SKILL.md STEP 4 and the STEP-5 checklist both have to shout about). The counterexample deliberately differs from `expected.json` in NOTHING but `source_span` (it carries no explicit `slug`), so no competing refusal can steal the exit. The `forbidden` half is the UNENFORCEABLE one, graded by census only: `тултип` is UI chrome and `таймаут`/`ретрай` are terms the source merely USES rather than EXPLAINS — every mechanical gate accepts them, and STEP 1 of the SKILL is the only thing standing between them and a permanent page. `Марина Гусева` is refused ONLY if the model honestly types `entity_type: person`; relabelled `concept` it sails through, so it too is census-graded. `retry_count` is half-covered: the underscore trips `INVALID_SLUG_CHARSET`, but the same schema column filed as `retry-count` is accepted by every validator in the rail.
